Light monochrome site with version-specific examples

recipes.title: Choose a data mode
recipes.summary: Static: local rows. Internal: the table fetches. External: your app fetches.
recipes.note: Internal mode expects { data: [...], recordsFiltered: total }. External callbacks and loading state belong to your app.

recipes.title: Show / hide columns
recipes.summary: Add a Columns button. Start fields hidden or keep important columns locked.
recipes.note: Use hiddenColumnIds + onHiddenColumnsChange for controlled visibility. A column's ID defaults to its data field.

recipes.title: CSV / Excel / PDF
recipes.summary: Choose the format, row scope and columns. Download a real file in one click.
recipes.code:
<Table mode="static" columns={columns} staticRows={rows}
  exportConfig={{
    fileName: 'people',
    formats: ['csv', 'xlsx', 'pdf'],
  }}
/>
recipes.note: Static exports include all filtered rows by default. Server mode exports loaded rows; add getRows for all matches. Action controls are excluded.

recipes.note: Use the downward chevron to open details; it points upward while open. Rows need stable IDs. Controlled state uses expandedRowIds + onExpandedChange.

recipes.title: Theme & className
recipes.summary: A white table with soft-black text and controls. Choose another base color when you need it.
recipes.code:
<Table mode="static" columns={columns} staticRows={rows}
  theme="#121212"
  className="people-table"
  style={{ padding: 16, borderRadius: 12 }}
  rowClassName={row => row.id === 0 ? 'featured-person' : undefined}
/>
recipes.note: The default is light. A hex theme such as #121212 changes the table palette; className and style customize its root.

recipes.title: Select rows
recipes.summary: Keep selected IDs in your state. Select one row or all filtered local rows.
recipes.note: Import useState from React. Server select-all covers the loaded page and preserves IDs selected on other pages.

recipes.title: Custom filters
recipes.summary: Put your controls beside search. You own their state and filtering logic.
recipes.note: Your custom filters own their state and styles. Use onClearFilters to reset them. Mobile opens them in a dialog.

recipes.title: Custom cells
recipes.summary: Use a renderer for buttons, badges or links. Keep exported values separate.
recipes.code: const columns: ColumnType[] = [ { data: 'name', title: 'Name', render: cell => {String(cell)} }, { id: 'actions', data: null, title: 'Actions', exportable: false, render: rowRenderer((_cell, row) => ) }, ];
recipes.note: Import rowRenderer from the package. Use exportValue: row => ... to format a plain export value without exporting the UI.

recipes.title: Next.js
recipes.summary: Import CSS globally. Put render functions and callbacks in a Client Component.
recipes.note: Import 'react-responsive-datatable-kit/styles.css' in app/layout.tsx or pages/_app.tsx. SSR stays enabled.

recipes.title: Props & troubleshooting
recipes.summary: Look up a prop, its default or a setup issue when you need it.

recipes.title: Loading & skeletons
recipes.summary: Show loading without changing column widths or creating a flashing horizontal scrollbar.
recipes.note: Pass your request loading state. Skeletons only fade; they do not scale. Reduced-motion preferences are respected.
